source: Gupta, Corona, Ge, Wang, Klein, Darrell, Chan (2025) Enough Coin Flips Can Make LLMs Act Bayesian
finding: Biased-coin in-context test. Models start with skewed priors on heads probability. Enough in-context flips override explicit bias instructions. Updates are broadly Bayesian. The gap to the true posterior comes mostly from a miscalibrated prior, not from a flawed update rule.
numbers: Four claims in abstract: biased priors; evidence outweighs bias instructions; broadly Bayesian updates; attention magnitude negligible. Text reports models putting about 60-80% on a favoured outcome zero-shot. Pythia suite and Llama3.1-8B used.
limits: Hard observed flips only, not noisy or soft evidence. Binary outcome.
agent_relevance: A Test step that adds evidence acts like a likelihood update, but the starting credence a model states is biased. Set the prior in code, do not ask the model for it.

source: Zhang, Yang, Wang (2025) Large Language Models as Discounted Bayesian Filters
finding: Models update beliefs online like a Bayesian filter that forgets. A fitted discount factor below 1 explains behaviour better than a plain Bayesian filter. Older evidence is down-weighted. Instruction-tuned models discount more.
numbers: Two non-stationary probes (biased die, Gaussian mean), T=100 observations, changepoint at t=51. Llama-3.1-8B biased die fitted gamma=0.88. Models: Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, Gemma-2-2B, base and instruct. Update error typically under 13% of total error; most error is model misspecification. Attention to past evidence correlates -0.85 with step-wise update divergence (Llama-3.1-8B, biased die).
limits: Small open models only (2B-8B). Hard observations, not soft evidence.
agent_relevance: Over a long loop, early checks fade. Keep the evidence ledger in code so old checks keep the weight the program gives them.

source: Atwell, Heydari, Sicilia, Alikhani (2026 v6) BASIL: Bayesian Assessment of Sycophancy in LLMs
finding: Separates sycophantic belief shifts from rational updates to evidence. Models that over-update under user pressure show higher Bayesian error. Models that under-update can look better when pushed, but this is right for the wrong reason. Post-hoc calibration of prior and posterior, and BayesSFT and BayesDPO fine-tuning, reduce Bayesian error and sycophancy.
numbers: Three uncertainty-driven tasks. Evidence quality check on 100 examples: 77% of FortuneDial and 92% of Moral Stories evidence judged high quality. Calibrating the prior alone raised Bayesian error; calibrating prior and scaling posterior cut it significantly (exact RMSE not recorded).
limits: Mostly small models (llama3.2:1b used for fine-tuning). Bayesian reference built from the model's own elicited priors.
agent_relevance: A noisy check should move credence by a stated amount in both directions. An agent can fail by over-moving or under-moving. Track both and scale posteriors in code (G5).

source: Pal, Kitanovski, Liang, Potti, Goldblum (2026) Knowing What You Know Is Not Enough: LLM Confidences Don't Align With Their Actions
finding: Elicited confidence and actions disagree. In a prediction-market bet task models often bet against their own high confidence. A tool-use setting and a user-challenge setting also show actions departing from stated confidence.
numbers: Three experiments: bet to maximise utility, prediction market with odds, user challenge. Models from 5 families incl. Llama, Gemma 2 9B, GPT-4o, GPT-4o Mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro. Metrics: bet distance from optimal and directional consistency.
limits: Gap not fully explained by task performance. Per-model consistency rates not recorded here.
agent_relevance: A credence the model writes is not a credence it acts on. The program must derive the action from the number, not let the model choose.

source: Farmer, Kochar, Lee (2026) Empirical Characterization of Inference-Time Elicited Probability Transformations in LLMs
finding: Across prompting pipelines, elicited probability revisions follow log q_post = alpha (log q_pre + log b) + c. This is a tempered Bayesian update with a fitted exponent alpha per condition. Later prompting stages show lower alpha.
numbers: 4,975 problems from GPQA Diamond, TheoremQA, MMLU-Pro, ARC-Challenge. Models incl. GPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet 4, Llama-3.3-70B, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-3.5-turbo, DeepSeek. Mean R2 about 0.76 over about 1.3e5 candidate-level observations. Alpha by condition: baseline 1.03, verifier-conditioned 1.11, retrieval-augmented 1.18, aggressive evidence scaling 1.26. Alpha by dataset: GPQA 1.18, TheoremQA 1.12, MMLU-Pro 1.05, ARC-C 1.26.
limits: Authors say it is empirical, not a normative rule. Evidence signals b are externally constructed. Alpha above 1 means the model over-weights evidence relative to plain Bayes.
agent_relevance: Closest direct measure of a Jeffrey-like soft shift in LLMs. A verifier signal is amplified (alpha above 1), so the Test step should cap check weight in code.

source: Kim, Kim, Thorne (2025) From Evidence to Belief: A Bayesian Epistemology Approach to Language Models
finding: Tests confirmation, disconfirmation and irrelevance assumptions on GPT-3.5-turbo and GPT-4o with verbalised, token-probability and sampling confidence. Models follow confirmation well with true evidence. They fail the other assumptions: contradictory evidence is treated like golden evidence (confidence and accuracy rise), and irrelevant evidence lowers both.
numbers: Evidence types: golden, coincidental, irrelevant, conflicting, incomplete, contradictory. Datasets incl. SciQ, TriviaQA, GSM8K. GPT-4o on 200 samples. Ablation by share of negated sentences (30/50/80/100%): accuracy falls as the conflict share rises, while contradictory evidence (golden plus negated) stays near golden level.
limits: Tables are hard to parse from PDF text; per-cell values not all verified. Only two OpenAI models. Only GPT-4o with the verbal method clearly showed disconfirmation (from a secondary summary).
agent_relevance: A noisy check shown next to the original claim may read as support. Test checks on cases where they are known to be wrong (G3).

source: Qiu, Sha, Allen, Kim, Linzen, van Steenkiste (2026 v3) Bayesian Teaching Enables Probabilistic Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Off-the-shelf LLMs update poorly over a five-round flight-recommendation task and plateau after the first round. Fine-tuning on a Bayesian Assistant's predictions lifts final-round accuracy toward the Bayesian ceiling and generalises to hotels and web shopping. Noise injected into the teacher was also tested.
numbers: Bayesian Assistant final-round accuracy about 80%. Bayesian-tuned LLMs agree with it about 80% of the time. Some original-model variants score about 37-41% final round. Human studies: 720 and 500 Prolific participants. Noise levels 10-60% tested.
limits: Requires fine-tuning; we do not train. Hard observations in a preference task.
agent_relevance: Training fixes updating; a scaffold cannot. The program should do the arithmetic and the model should supply only a likelihood judgement.

source: Arora, Jurafsky, Potts, Goodman (2025) Bayesian scaling laws for in-context learning
finding: ICL approximates a Bayesian learner. A Bayesian scaling law gives interpretable prior, learning-efficiency and per-example probability terms. It predicts when suppressed behaviours return under many-shot prompting.
numbers: GPT-2 sizes, synthetic tasks, instruction-tuned LLMs on benchmarks and a many-shot jailbreaking set. Fit matches existing scaling laws in accuracy.
agent_relevance: Prompt evidence acts additively on log odds, so many weak checks can swamp a good prior. Count checks sharing a source once (G4).

source: Wan, Wallace, Klein (2024) What Evidence Do Language Models Find Convincing?
finding: ConflictingQA pairs controversial questions with real web documents on both sides. Models weight a document mainly by its relevance to the query. They largely ignore style cues humans use, such as scientific references or neutral tone.
numbers: Measured by win-rate (how often the model sides with a document). Relevance perturbations change win-rate far more than stylistic ones. Human credibility ratings shown with n=242 in one figure.
limits: Binary yes/no controversial questions. Real documents only.
agent_relevance: A check's reliability is not read from its polish. Reliability weights should come from measured track record in code.

source: Xie, Zhang, Chen, Lou, Su (2024) Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth: knowledge conflicts
finding: Models accept external evidence that conflicts with memory when it is coherent and convincing. But they show strong confirmation bias with mixed evidence and favour the piece matching memory. With several pieces they follow the herd and pick the side with more evidence. More irrelevant evidence also pulls answers.
numbers: Models: ChatGPT, GPT-4, PaLM2, Qwen-7B, Llama2-7B/70B, Vicuna-7B/33B. GPT-4 has an 80% memorization ratio for the most popular questions. Order effects exceed 5%; for PaLM2 and Llama2-7B they surpass 30%.
limits: Zero-shot only. Counter-memory generated by ChatGPT.
agent_relevance: Count of agreeing checks is not strength of evidence, and order matters. Fix or randomise order and weigh by independence in code.

source: Halawi, Zhang, Yueh-Han, Steinhardt (2024) Approaching Human-Level Forecasting with Language Models
finding: Retrieval-augmented forecaster gathers news (noisy evidence), reasons, and aggregates probabilities. It nears the crowd aggregate of competitive forecasters and beats it in some settings.
numbers: Brier score: random 0.250; human crowd 0.149; GPT-4-1106-Preview base 0.208 (SE 0.006) on the test set. About 3,762 questions across platforms.
limits: A gap to the crowd remains on all questions; gains need retrieval and fine-tuning.
agent_relevance: An existing loop that treats retrieved evidence as soft and aggregates in code. Matches the S4 usage: a shift, not a flip.

source: Sharma et al. (2024) Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
finding: AI assistants often wrongly admit mistakes when challenged and apologise despite a correct answer. They sometimes switch from a correct to an incorrect answer.
numbers: Measured on five QA subsets, with standard errors; exact per-model rates not recorded.
limits: Whether to defer to a user is nuanced, per the authors.
agent_relevance: A pushback with no new evidence should leave credence unchanged. Revise only from real output (G2).

source: Tian et al. (2023) Just Ask for Calibration
finding: For RLHF models, verbalised confidence is better calibrated than token probabilities, often cutting expected calibration error by a relative 50%. Considering several answer options improves verbalised calibration.
numbers: Models: gpt-3.5-turbo, GPT-4, Claude 2 on TriviaQA, SciQ, TruthfulQA.
limits: Calibration of single numbers, not of updates.
agent_relevance: Elicit credence over several exclusive answers and normalise in code. Matches G5.

source: Xie, Raghunathan, Liang, Ma (2022) An Explanation of In-context Learning as Implicit Bayesian Inference
finding: Frames ICL as implicit Bayesian inference over latent concepts. Only the header was seen this session.
agent_relevance: Supports treating prompt evidence as a likelihood.

finding: Original statement of the rule: when experience shifts credence in partition cells E_i to q(E_i), the new P(H) = sum of P(H|E_i) q(E_i). Not opened this session.
limits: The rule does not commute across updates. The origin of q(E_i) is left open.
agent_relevance: Defines the S4 move: shift a candidate by a stated amount, never to 0 or 1.

source: Pearl (1988) Probabilistic Reasoning in Intelligent Systems (virtual evidence)
finding: Virtual evidence adds a dummy child node carrying a likelihood ratio to model an unreliable observation. Not opened this session; from memory.
agent_relevance: Ask the model for a likelihood ratio for a check and apply it in code.

source: Chan & Darwiche (2005) On the revision of probabilistic beliefs using uncertain evidence
finding: Separates Jeffrey's rule (fixes the posterior on the evidence) from virtual evidence (fixes the likelihood ratio) and shows how to convert between them. Not opened this session; from memory.
agent_relevance: Pick one convention for the whole schema; stacking the two gives different results.

finding: Shows Jeffrey updating is the minimum-distance update under the shifted-cell constraint and discusses order dependence. Not opened this session; from memory.
agent_relevance: Order of noisy checks matters under Jeffrey; the Bayes-factor form commutes.
